readerQuestionCoverage.item: Do scar removal creams actually work?
readerQuestionCoverage.whyThisMatters: Managing user expectations about over-the-counter creams prevents wasting money on ineffective products.
readerQuestionCoverage.finalCopyUse: Deconstruct the difference between flat color marks (PIH/PIE) which creams can fade, and structural pitted craters which they cannot fill.

readerQuestionCoverage.item: Is silicone gel effective for acne scars?
readerQuestionCoverage.whyThisMatters: Silicone gel is clinically validated only for raised (hypertrophic/keloid) scars, not pitted craters.
readerQuestionCoverage.finalCopyUse: Detail the clinical mechanism of silicone (hydration, occlusion, collagen regulation) and its target scar types.

recommendationSanityPlan.item: Kojic Acid / Alpha Arbutin for post-acne dark marks (PIH)
recommendationSanityPlan.whyThisMatters: Tyrosinase inhibitors are the most effective over-the-counter actives for hyperpigmentation.
recommendationSanityPlan.finalCopyUse: Outline standard concentrations and how to layer them safely.

claimRiskPlan.item: Onion extract is a miracle cure for pitted craters
claimRiskPlan.whyThisMatters: Overstating onion extract's efficacy leads to false hopes.
claimRiskPlan.finalCopyUse: Soften the claim by stating onion extract has mild anti-inflammatory properties that help flatten raised surgical scars but does nothing for atrophic craters.

troubleshootingPlan.item: What to do if a scar cream causes breakouts
troubleshootingPlan.whyThisMatters: Heavy occlusive scar creams (often containing heavy oils or silicones) can clog pores on acne-prone skin.
troubleshootingPlan.finalCopyUse: Advise checking for comedogenic ingredients and switching to lightweight gel formulations.
